latin: Ordo librorum naturalis philosophiae ab Aristotele tradite est iste: Liber Physicorum, coeli et mundi, de generatione, metheororum, mineralium, de plantis, de generatione animalium, de partibus animalium, de progressu animalium, de anima, tum libri qui dicuntur parui naturales.
latin_note: The sheet's line-break slash in 'metheororum,/mineralium' is repaired to a comma-and-space. 1486 reads 'ab Aristotle est iste' (omitting 'tradite'); the Emendationes errorum inserts 'tradite', giving the reading followed here, which (unlike other emendations in this stretch) the 1487 reprint adopted.
translation: This is the sequence of the books of natural philosophy that Aristotle handed on: Physics, De caelo et mundo, De generatione, Meteorologica, De mineralibus, De plantis, De generatione animalium, De partibus animalium, De progressu animalium, De anima, and then what are called the Parva naturalia.
